title: Jorgensen 2003a: csa fibre corrected of paraspinal / lumbar extensor mass at L3-L4 (F, lateral_recumbent)
muscle_as_reported: right lumbar back muscles (combined iliocostalis, longissimus, multifidus)

imaging.modality: MRI 0.3 T Hitachi Airis open, T1 (TR 400, TE 10)
imaging.plane: axial slices through and PARALLEL to each lumbar intervertebral disc (L1-L2..L5-S1)
imaging.posture_detail: lying on LEFT side (lateral recumbent) on pegboard, torso flexion 0/15/30/45 deg (S1-C7 line), knees extended, padding against coronal sag

quantity.name: csa_fibre_corrected
quantity.definition: anatomical CSA multiplied by cosine of fibre angle to the plane normal (authors may call it PCSA/physiological area; NOT volume/fibre-length PCSA); authors call it ACSA: raw CSA x dot product of scan-plane normal with literature fascicle direction (Macintosh & Bogduk 1991 coronal; Macintosh 1993 sagittal, interpolated for 15/30 deg)

source.authors: Jorgensen MJ, Marras WS, Gupta P
source.sample: 24 healthy subjects (12 M, 12 F); young healthy adults

protocol.summary: Open 0.3 T MRI, lateral recumbent with controlled torso flexion; right lumbar back muscle outlined at each disc level, fibre-angle corrected.
how_to_simulate: Put the model in lateral-recumbent (gravity sideways) posture with 45 deg torso flexion; match the measured lumbar lordosis (L1-S1 19.2 deg, L1-L5 15.8 deg mean, Jorgensen 2003b Table 2).
Cut a plane through the L3-L4 disc centre parallel to the disc mid-plane.

Sum the PCSA of the RIGHT longissimus + iliocostalis + multifidus fascicles crossing that plane (the measured area is raw MRI area x cos(fascicle angle to the plane normal) using literature fascicle angles, i.e. approx. the PCSA of fibres crossing the slice).
Compare with the measured mean +/- SD.
protocol.notes: Fascicle angles in Table 1 are literature inputs (Macintosh & Bogduk 1991; Macintosh et al. 1993), not measured here. cm2 -> mm2 (x100).

extraction.check_notes: Table 2 text layout is unambiguous; values re-read against the PDF text and page 283 render.
